title: return relevant catalog products for a storefront search
input: The storefront supplies the permitted search query, catalog context and customer-consent settings.
action: Commerce Search retrieves and ranks supported products using the configured catalog and serving settings. Catalog ingestion and events influence available results; the commerce backend checks current price and purchase availability.
output: The storefront displays validated product results and sends checkout to its separate transaction backend.
check: Test stale catalog entries, ranking relevance, inventory reconciliation and sensitive-user-event handling.

title: train a large model with a coordinated accelerator architecture
input: The ML team specifies the training framework, accelerator topology, network and shared dataset requirements.
action: AI Hypercomputer combines supported compute, accelerator, networking and software capabilities for AI workloads. The selected training runtime distributes the actual computation; topology and storage access are configured explicitly.
output: The training pipeline stores accepted model checkpoints outside temporary workers and evaluates the resulting model.
check: Test distributed startup, checkpoint recovery, dataset throughput and actual accelerator utilization before scaling the training run.

title: review a provider access request before granting the selected access
input: The customer access owner receives a supported access request with its reason, scope and expiry.
action: Access Approval requests customer approval for covered Google personnel access under the configured settings and supported exceptions. The approver assesses the requested access; approval does not change end-user application permissions.
output: The owner approves only the justified request or rejects it and retains the related operational context.
check: Verify the requested scope, approval expiry and associated access evidence under the service's coverage and exception rules.

title: define an access level used by a protected service policy
input: The security owner defines the required device, network or identity-related access conditions.
action: Access Context Manager stores supported access levels and perimeter-related policy configuration. An integrating enforcement service evaluates the applicable policy; the policy manager does not proxy application requests.
output: The owner associates the reviewed access level with the chosen supported enforcement policy.
check: Test allowed and denied contexts through the actual integrating service and inspect effective inherited policy.

title: review covered provider access to customer data
input: The compliance owner selects the supported resources, investigation window and authorized log readers.
action: Access Transparency supplies records for covered Google personnel access to customer content under its supported scope. The records describe access evidence; they do not block access or replace Access Approval.
output: The auditor correlates the recorded access with support requests and approved operational activity.
check: Check coverage, log fields and exceptions before concluding that the selected provider access was fully accounted for.

title: assign a relevant service advisory to its workload owner
input: The operations owner identifies the organization scope and the advisory requiring action.
action: Advisory Notifications delivers supported advisory information for the configured organization or resources. The notification identifies a condition or recommended action; the receiving team validates its workload relevance.
output: The assigned owner schedules and performs the required approved resource change.
check: Verify affected resources, advisory status and actual application behavior after the action before closing the work item.

title: analyze an approved camera stream through a configured vision application
input: The site owner selects authorized camera streams, analysis components and permitted output destinations.
action: The vision platform ingests the selected stream and runs the configured supported application components. Their analytics produce the requested observations; camera consent and pipeline configuration determine the collected data.
output: The operations application consumes accepted observations and routes uncertain detections for review.
check: Test stream interruption, timestamp alignment, detection quality and access to identifiable video content.

title: operate a PostgreSQL-compatible application on a customer-managed host
input: The database owner chooses the supported Omni version, host capacity and protected data volumes.
action: AlloyDB Omni supplies the supported downloadable database engine running on the selected infrastructure. The engine executes compatible SQL; the owner manages hosting, networking, backups and the chosen availability arrangement.
output: The application commits accepted transactions through its restricted database connection.
check: Test feature compatibility, concurrency, backup restoration and host failure before accepting the database deployment.

title: prioritize financial activity for investigator review
input: The compliance team prepares the supported financial data model and permitted investigation labels.
action: AML AI's configured workflow analyzes eligible financial activity to produce risk-oriented outputs. Dataset quality and training or evaluation configuration determine usefulness; investigators make the regulated case disposition.
output: The financial crime team reviews prioritized activity with transaction evidence and records its justified decision.
check: Evaluate known cases, false positives, data lineage and access controls before incorporating outputs into investigation queues.

title: protect and route a partner order API
input: The partner submits an authorized HTTPS order request with the agreed token and payload schema.
action: Apigee applies the configured API proxy policies, such as token validation, quota and request transformation, then routes the accepted request to the backend. The backend performs order validation and persistence.
output: The backend returns the accepted order result through the proxy's configured response policies.
check: Test invalid tokens, quota exhaustion, backend timeout and unsafe transformations before exposing the partner API.
